title: 3D Bioprinting of Murine Cortical Astrocytes for Engineering Neural-Like Tissue
protocol: Transfer 10 mL of cold Hanks Buffered Salt Solution (HBSS) to a 100 mm culture dish and keep it on ice.
Transfer 1 mL of HBSS to a 1.5 mL microtube for each animal and keep the tube on ice.
Prepare astrocytes culture medium using DMEM F12 + 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 2% glutamine, and 1% penicillin-streptomycin (P/S).
Sterilize the medium by filtering it through a 0.2 µm filter.
Euthanize C57Bl/6 mice pups (postnatal day 1) by decapitation using a sharp operating scissor.
Pull the skin with forceps and expose the skull of the mouse pup.
Cut the skull from the foramen magnum to the top of the head along the sagittal plane using a sharp curved tip scissor.
Lift the brain from the cranial cavity and place it in the culture dish containing 10 mL of cold HBSS with a sterilized spatula.
Place the culture dish under a stereomicroscope, and use two blunt-tip forceps to remove meninges from the brain.
Separate the cortices from the rest of the brain by gently rolling them away using a spatula.
Transfer the cortices to a microtube containing 1 mL of cold HBSS.
Cut the cortical tissue into small pieces under laminar flow using curved scissors.
Wash the tissue with 1 mL of HBSS by pipetting up and down three times.
Repeat washing process two more times, discarding HBSS each time.
Incubate the tissue with 1 mL of 0.05% trypsin at 37 °C for 5 minutes.
Gently pipette up and down 15 times to mechanically dissociate the tissue.
Transfer the solution to a 15 mL conical tube.
Neutralize trypsin activity by adding an equal volume of FBS.
Filter the solution through a cell strainer filter of 0.4 µm.
Wash the filter with 1 mL of astrocytes medium and collect the cell suspension.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 minutes at 200 x g and 25 °C.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Suspend the pellet in 1 mL of astrocytes culture medium.
Transfer the cell suspension to a T25 culture flask.
Make up the volume of the medium to 3.5 mL.
Incubate the cells at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Replace the medium after 24 hours if cells are adherent.
Change the medium every 3 days.
Wash the cells with 2 mL of 1x PBS after 7 days.
Remove microglia and oligodendrocytes by washing.
Replace PBS solution with astrocyte culture medium.
Leave the culture flask in an orbital shaker at 180 rpm overnight.
Weigh 10 g of gelatin from porcine skin.
Dissolve gelatin in 100 mL of PBS on a heating plate at 240 rpm and 50°C.
Add 2 mL of methacrylic anhydride under a hood for functionalization.
Let the gelatin emulsion stir at 240 rpm and 50°C for 2 hours.
Avoid breathing dust/fume/gas/mist/vapour/spray when handling MA.
Rinse cautiously with water for several minutes if MA gets in eyes, remove contact lenses if present and easy to do, continue rinsing, then call a POISON CENTER/doctor.
Call a POISON CENTER/doctor if you feel unwell after swallowing MA; rinse mouth.
Add MA very slowly drop by drop.
Dilute the gelatin-MA solution in 100 mL of preheated PBS (50 °C) to obtain 200 mL of final volume and let the solution stir at 240 rpm and 50 °C for 10 min.
Soak dialysis membrane (molecular cutoff 12-14 kDa) in deionized water until it is soft.
Fill membranes with deionized water to ensure there are no holes or defects.
Transfer the gelatin-MA solution to the membranes using a funnel, closing both sides leaving extra space inside.
Place membranes containing the gelatin-MA solution into a container with 2 L of distilled water for dialysis, letting them stir at 40 °C for 5 days (500 rpm).
Cover the container to avoid water evaporation during dialysis.
Change distilled water two times in a day.
Flip membranes upside down for homogenization each time.
On the fifth day, mix 200 mL of preheated ultrapure water (40 °C) with dialyzed gelatin-MA and stir at 40 °C for 15 min.
Transfer the gelatin-MA solution to 50 mL conical tubes up to 25 mL and store at -80°C for 2 days.
Store the tubes horizontally to facilitate lyophilization.
Lyophilize the frozen solutions for 3-5 days.
Store the lyophilized GelMA protected from humidity.
Prepare saline solution (NaCl 0.9%) in deionized water.
Dissolve 10 mg of fibrinogen from bovine plasma in 1 mL of saline solution to obtain a concentration of 10 mg/mL.
Agitate the solution at 37 °C until complete dissolution of fibrinogen.
Use a rotary system placed inside an oven or magnetic agitation on a hot plate at 180 rpm for fibrinogen dissolution.
Weigh 0.12 g of gelatin.
Add gelatin to 1.9 mL of preheated PBS (40 °C).
Vortex to facilitate dissolution of gelatin.
Keep the emulsion at 40 °C until complete dissolution.
Weigh 0.06 g of lyophilized GelMA and transfer to the gelatin solution.
Vortex to facilitate dissolution of GelMA.
Keep the solution at 40 °C until complete dissolution.
Pipette 0.9 mL of the 10 mg/mL fibrinogen solution and transfer to the gelatin/GelMA solution.
Weigh 0.015 g of photoinitiator (PI) and transfer to the gelatin/GelMA/fibrinogen solution.
Mix the solution by flipping the tube up and down.
Keep the solution at 40 °C protected from light to avoid PI degradation.
Store the bioink at 4 °C for a maximum of 24 hours.
Filter the solution using a 0.2 µm filter under laminar flow into a sterile 15 mL conical tube.
Transfer 980 µL of the biomaterial solution to a 15 mL conical tube.
Dilute laminin in saline solution to obtain a stock solution of 100 µg/mL.
Pipette 20 µL of laminin and transfer to the tube containing the bioink.
Mix gently by pipetting up and down, avoiding bubbles.
If any bubbles persist, centrifuge the conical tube at 200 x g for 2 min.
Trypsinize primary astrocytes with 0.05% trypsin for 5 min.
Neutralize the trypsin activity with FBS at a ratio of 1:1 and transfer the cells to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 x g for 5 min.
Count the cells and transfer 1 x 10^6 cells to a different conical tube.
Centrifuge the new tube at 200 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant leaving a small volume (~200 µL) to suspend the cell pellet, by gently tapping the bottom of the conical tube.
Transfer 1 mL of gelatin/GelMA/fibrinogen solution to the tube containing the cells and gently pipette up and down to homogenize, obtaining a final concentration of 1 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Prepare a stock solution of thrombin 100 U/mL in sterile deionized water with 0.1% (w/v) bovine serum albumin (BSA) in a 15 mL conical tube.
Store the thrombin stock in microtubes at -20 °C.
Pipette 100 µL of thrombin stock solution and transfer to a 50 mL conical tube containing 8.9 mL of sterile deionized water to obtain a final concentration of 1 U/mL thrombin.
Prepare a 10% (w/v) CaCl2 solution in deionized water and sterilize using a 0.2 µm filter.
Transfer 1.1 mL of the 10% CaCl2 solution to the conical tube containing thrombin, obtaining a final ratio of 1:9 (CaCl2 to thrombin).
Expose the bioprinter to UV light for 15 min and wipe it down with ethanol 70%.
Turn on the bioprinter using the power switch.
Connect the machine to the computer through a USB cable.
Open the controlling software to connect it to the bioprinter and load the file design.
Transfer the astrocytes-laden gelatin/GelMA/fibrinogen bioink to a 5 mL plastic syringe using a 1,000 µL pipette slowly.
Leave the syringe at 4 °C for 2 min.
Connect a sterile 22 G blunt needle to the syringe.
Connect the syringe to the bioprinter printhead and manually flush the bioink to remove remaining bubbles.
Place a 35 mm culture dish on the bioprinter table.
Position the needle 0.1 mm away from the culture dish surface.
Press the Print button.
Ensure that the syringe moves away from the dish once printing is complete.
Close the culture dish after printing.
Place the culture dish under UV light at 2 mW/cm2 for 2 x 60 s (up and down) for GelMA crosslinking.
Transfer the bioprinted construct to a 24-well plate using a sterile spatula under laminar flow conditions.
Add 500 μL of thrombin/CaCl2 solution to allow fibrin crosslinking.
Remove the crosslinking solution after 30 minutes.
Wash the construct with 2 mL of PBS 1x.
Replace the PBS with 1 mL of astrocytes culture medium.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Change the medium every 3 days.
Transfer the bioprinted construct to a 35 mm culture dish using a spatula.
Wash the construct with 1 mL of 1x PBS.
Deposit 100 μL of the Live/Dead reagent over the construct.
Keep it at 37 °C for 30 min, protected from light.
Remove the Live/Dead reagent after incubation.
Wash the construct with 1 mL of 1x PBS.
Transfer the sample to a confocal dish using a spatula.
Observe the cells within the construct under a confocal microscope using 488 and 570 nm excitation for image acquisition.
Seed 0.5 x 10^6 astrocytes (passage 1-3) in a 35 mm confocal dish, add astrocytes medium, and incubate them at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Remove the culture medium when cells are confluent and wash with 1 mL of 1x PBS.
Deposit 200 μL of the Live/Dead reagent on the dish and keep it at 37 °C for 30 min, protected from light.
Remove the Live/Dead reagent and wash the cells with 1 mL of 1x PBS.
Take the dish to a confocal microscope coupled with a digital camera, and use 488 and 570 nm excitation for image acquisition.
Calculate the number of viable (green) and dead (red) using computational software.
Remove the medium from the well.
Wash the construct with 1 mL of 3x PBS.
Add 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS to the well until the construct is completely covered.
Leave the PFA-covered construct for 2 h at 4 °C.
Remove the PFA and wash the construct with 1 mL of 3x PBS.
Treat the sample with glycine 0.1 mol/L for 5 min.
Wash the sample with 1 mL of 1x PBS for 5 min, 3 times.
Permeabilize the sample with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 and 10% FBS for 1 h at 25 °C under orbital agitation.
Incubate the construct with chicken anti-GFAP (primary antibody dilution 1:500) at 4 °C overnight.
Aspirate the primary antibody and wash the sample with 1 mL of PBS for 5 min, 3 times.
Incubate the sample with Alexa fluor 488-conjugated anti-chicken (secondary antibody dilution 1:500) and 1 μg/mL DAPI for 1 h at 25 °C under orbital agitation.
Wash the sample with 1 mL of PBS for 5 min, 3 times.
Transfer the construct to a 35 mm confocal dish.
Seed 0.5 x 10^6 astrocytes (passage 1-3) in a 35 mm confocal dish.
Add astrocyte medium and incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until cells are confluent.
Remove the culture medium when cells are confluent.
Wash the confluent astrocytes with 1 mL of 1x PBS.
Repeat steps 8.1.2-8.1.10 for GFAP staining.
Add 200 µL of 50 µg/mL fluorescent-conjugated phalloidin solution in PBS.
Add 1 µg/mL DAPI to the construct.
Incubate for 1 h at 25 °C under orbital agitation, protected from light.
Wash the sample with 1 mL of PBS for 5 min three times.
Transfer the construct to a confocal dish using a spatula.
Seal the dish to prevent drying out.
Take the dishes to a confocal microscope coupled with a digital camera.
Image the samples at excitation wavelengths of 359 nm, 488 nm, and 570 nm.
Use magnification of 10x for overall visualization.
Use magnification of 40x or 63x for zoomed images of cells.
